title: Where saving company interrupts judgment
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 256
summary: The shabad looks squarely at judgment that no one can block, then names the saving turn: join Saadh Sangat, remember Hari, and let holy company interrupt the loneliness of condemnation.
whyItMatters: It matters when guilt or exposure makes the soul feel already sentenced. The verse does not leave the person alone before judgment; it sends them into remembered company where the Lord's Name is still being held.
takeaway: Enter the company where remembrance can outlast judgment.

lines.gurmukhi: ਢਾਹਨ ਲਾਗੇ ਧਰਮ ਰਾਇ ਕਿਨਹਿ ਨ ਘਾਲਿਓ ਬੰਧ ॥
lines.transliteration: ddaahan laage dharam rai kineh na ghaalio ba(n)dh ||
lines.translation: When the Righteous Judge of Dharma begins to destroy someone, no one can place any obstacle in His Way.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਉਬਰੇ ਜਪਿ ਹਰੀ ਸਾਧਸੰਗਿ ਸਨਬੰਧ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: naanak ubare jap haree saadhasa(n)g sanaba(n)dh ||1||
lines.translation: O Nanak, those who join the Saadh Sangat and meditate on the Lord are saved. ||1||

structure: The shabad begins by naming the helplessness of standing before judgment.
From there it turns toward the company where remembrance is still alive.
The closing movement rests by showing that salvation is received in Sangat, not manufactured alone.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad looks squarely at judgment that no one can block, then names the saving turn: join Saadh Sangat, remember Hari, and let holy company interrupt the loneliness of condemnation.
evidence.turn: The turn is from private exposure before judgment into Saadh Sangat, where remembrance of Hari becomes saving company.
evidence.practicalImplication: Do not let guilt isolate you. Enter the company where the Lord's Name is remembered before judgment becomes the only voice you hear.
